newsitem.title: USA: Unidentified prints found on Atlanta bomb letter.
newsitem.headline: Unidentified prints found on Atlanta bomb letter.

text.p: Federal agents investigating a series of bombings in Atlanta have found unidentified fingerprints on a letter claiming responsibility for two attacks, a source close to the investigation said Monday.

The 2-1/2 page handwritten letter, purported to be from a violent anti-abortion group called The Army of God, claimed responsibility for the bombing of an Atlanta abortion clinic in January and a gay nightclub in February.
No one was killed in either blast but at least a dozen people were injured.
Four separately written copies of the letter were mailed to news organisations, including Reuters, within hours of the nightclub bombing Feb. 21.
The letter threatened "total war" against the federal government and contained a special code to be used for establishing the group's identity in future bombings.
The source said two unidentified prints turned up on the copy sent to Reuters during forensic testing. "Maybe this is the print we're looking for," the source said.
The letter showed eight fingerprints altogether. Six of the eight belonged to the journalist who opened the envelope containing the letter.
A spokesman for the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms (ATF) had no comment, and the FBI in Atlanta did not return phone calls.
News of the fingerprints came two weeks after the FBI released excerpts of the Army of God letter in hopes of eliciting clues from the general public.

FBI investigators said they believed the author's claim of involvement in the abortion clinic and nightclub bombings. Each attack involved a second "sucker" bomb intended for law enforcement agents and emergency workers who swarmed to the scenes after the initial explosion.

There also have been growing convictions among investigators about a possible link between the two attacks and the Olympic park bombing, which left two people dead and more than 100 injured last July.
